newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo c.banker says banking system must reconstruct.
newsitem.headline: Yugo c.banker says banking system must reconstruct.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank on Monday called for a reconstruction of the banking system to make it more efficient and responsive to the economy's increasing financial needs.
"With the banking sector as it is, we cannot provide sufficient financial support for the industry," National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic said.

"I purposely call for reconstruction of the banking system because it has not been done since 1994 when the government launched the programme of monetary reconstruction," he told a gathering of bankers and businessmen.
In January 1994, after a year of the world's highest inflation running at 60 percent a day, banks were left with no deposits, only with buildings and employees.
Banovic blamed strong inflationary movements for the lack of deposits and said now that the inflation was curbed, banks had to reform to survive. Banks will be cleared of dubious assets.
He insisted banks would have to cover losses incurred over past two years by themselves. "If not, there will be only two ways out: to close down or to merge with a healthier bank."
He acknowledged that liquidity of the banks and companies deteriorated during 1996, but insisted it was not due to the central bank's tough monetary stance.

The central bank will push for a development of the local financial market and will on its part create new instruments to finance production. This will make classical commercial lending of the banking sector a matter of the past, Banovic said.
